Commentary of al-Tha'alabi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 64, verses 9–18:

﴿Yawma yajma'ukum﴾: the common reading (qira'at al-'ammah) is with the *ya'* (ي), in accordance with His saying, ﴿So believe in Allah and His Messenger, and in the light which We have sent down. And Allah is Acquainted with what you do﴾. Ruways, on the authority of Ya'qub, read *nafjama'ukum* (نجمعكم) with the *nun* (ن), taking as the basis His saying ﴿We have sent down﴾.

﴿For the Day of Assembly. That is the Day of Mutual Loss (yawm al-taghabun)﴾. *Al-taghabun* is a *tafa'ul* form from *al-ghabn* (الغبن), which means the loss of one's share. The intended meaning is clear. A report about the explanation of *al-taghabun* has come from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ):

Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad informed us, saying: Musa ibn Muhammad ibn 'Ali related to us, saying: 'Abd Allah ibn Muhammad ibn Sinan related to us, saying: Kathir ibn Yahya related to us, saying: Abu Amina ibn Mu'alla al-Thaqafi related to us, saying: Sa'id ibn Abi Sa'id al-Minqari related to us, from Abu Hurayah, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "There is no believing servant who enters Paradise except that his place in the Fire is shown to him, so that if he had done evil he would increase in gratitude. And there is no servant who enters the Fire except that his place in Paradise is shown to him, so that if he had done good he would increase in regret." [316] [[Kanz al-'Ummal: 14/481, no. 39346.]]

The exegetes said: Whoever is cheated by his people of his dwellings in Paradise, then on that day the loss of every disbeliever will become manifest, through the blessing of faith, and the loss of every believer through his shortcoming in good deeds and his squandering of his days.

﴿And whoever believes in Allah and does righteous deeds, He will remove from him his misdeeds and admit him into gardens beneath which rivers flow, abiding therein forever. That is the great triumph.﴾ The people of Medina and Syria read *nukaffir* and *nudkhiluhu* (نكفّر وندخله) here and in the surah that follows it, with the *nun* (ن); the rest read them with the *ya'* (ي).

﴿But those who disbelieve and deny Our signs — those are the companions of the Fire, abiding therein forever, and wretched is the destination.﴾ ﴿No calamity strikes except by the permission of Allah﴾, that is, by His will and decree.

﴿And whoever believes in Allah — He guides his heart﴾. They meant by this: whoever believes in Allah, that no calamity strikes him except by the permission of Allah, [then] He guides his heart: He grants him success in certainty, until he knows that what befell him would not have missed him, and what missed him would not have befallen him. This was said by Ibn 'Abbas.

Al-Hasan ibn Ya'qub, through an authorization (ijazah) from 'Abd Allah ibn Hamid, informed me, saying: Abu Ishaq Ibrahim ibn 'Abd Allah related to us, saying: Waki' related to us, from al-A'mash, from Abu Zabyan, who said: We used to present the copies of the Qur'an to 'Alqama ibn Qays, and he passed by this verse: ﴿No calamity strikes except by the permission of Allah, and whoever believes in Allah — He guides his heart﴾. We asked him about it, and he said: It is the man who is struck by a calamity and knows that it is from Allah, so he is content and submits.

Abu Bakr al-Warraq said: ﴿And whoever believes in Allah﴾ at the time of blessing and ease, so that he knows it is from the bounty of Allah — ﴿He guides his heart﴾ to gratitude. And ﴿whoever believes in Allah﴾ at the time of hardship and affliction, so that he knows it is from Allah — ﴿He guides his heart﴾ to contentment and patience.

Abu 'Uthman al-Jiri said: Whoever's faith is sound, ﴿He guides his heart﴾ to follow the Sunnah.

The reciters differed regarding this verse. The common reading is *yahdi qalbahu* (يَهْدِ قَلْبَهُ) with a *fath*a on the *ya'* and on the *ba'*, which was chosen by Abu 'Ubayd and Abu Hatim. Al-Sulami read it with a *damma* on the *ya'* and on the *ba'* and a *fath*a on the *dal*, as the passive verb. Talha ibn Musarrif read *nahdi qalbahu* (نهد قلبه) with the *nun* and a *fath*a on the *ba'*, as a form of exaltation (ta'zim).

Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, saying: Ibn Hamdan related to us, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Faraj the reciter related to us, saying: Abu 'Umar the reciter related to us, saying: Abu 'Umara related to us, saying: Sahl ibn Musa al-Aswari related to us, saying: Someone informed me who heard 'Ikrima reading: *wa man yu'min billahi yahda'* (ومن يؤمن بالله يهدأ قلبه), from *al-hudu'*, meaning he becomes calm and tranquil.

Malik ibn Dinar read *yahda qalbuhu* (يهدا قلبه) with a soft *alif* in place of the *hamza*.

﴿And Allah is Knowing of everything.﴾ ﴿And obey Allah and obey the Messenger. But if you turn away, then upon Our Messenger is only the clear conveyance﴾: the clear delivery (al-tabligh al-bayyin).

﴿Allah — there is no deity except Him. And upon Allah let the believers rely.﴾ ﴿O you who have believed, indeed, among your spouses and your children are enemies to you, so beware of them.﴾ It was revealed concerning a people who wanted to emigrate, but their spouses and children discouraged them from it.

Ibn 'Abbas said: A man would embrace Islam, and when he wanted to emigrate, his family and children would prevent him, saying to him: "We adjure you by Allah not to go and leave your family and kinsfolk and become in Medina without family or wealth. We have been patient with your Islam, but we will not be patient with your separation, and we will not go out with you." Some of them would be softened toward them and remain, and so would not emigrate. When he did emigrate, the people would find fault with them in religion, because they had delayed in emigrating. And some of them would not obey them, and they would say to them, in their disagreement over leaving: "If Allah gathers us and you, you will not get any good from me. I will certainly do this and that." So Allah the Exalted revealed this verse.

'Ata' ibn Yasar and 'Ata' al-Khurasani said: It was revealed concerning 'Awf ibn Malik al-Ash'ari, who had a family and children. Whenever he wanted to go on a raid, they would weep before him and soften him, saying: "To whom will you leave us, and abandon us?" So he would relent and stay. Then Allah the Exalted and Majestic revealed: ﴿O you who have believed, indeed, among your spouses and your children are enemies to you﴾, because they compelled you to disobedience and to abandoning obedience, ﴿so beware of them﴾, lest you accept from them.

﴿And if you pardon and overlook and forgive﴾, and do not punish them for their opposition to you, ﴿then indeed, Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.﴾ ﴿Your wealth and your children are only a trial (fitnah)﴾: a test and an examination that drives you to gain from the unlawful and to withhold from the truth. Al-Qutayabi said: *Ighram* (إغرام). It is said: "Fulan was tempted (futina) with such-and-such a woman," meaning he became infatuated with her.

The wise said: The particle *min* (من) for partition (tab'id) was used in mentioning the spouses and children when it reports their enmity, because not all of them are enemies. And *min* was not mentioned in His saying ﴿Indeed, your wealth and your children are only a trial﴾, because they are never free of trial and of the heart being occupied with them. This is shown by the saying of 'Abd Allah ibn Mas'ud: "Let none of you say, 'O Allah, I seek refuge in You from trial,' for there is none among you who returns to wealth, family and children without being encompassed by a trial. Rather, let him say: 'O Allah, I seek refuge in You from misleading trials.'" [[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 18/143.]]

Ibn Manjawayh informed us, saying: 'Umar ibn al-Khattab related to us, saying: 'Abd Allah ibn al-Fadl related to us, saying: Abu Khaythama related to us, saying: Zayd ibn Habbab related to us, saying: Husayn ibn Waqid, judge of Marw, related to us, saying: 'Abd Allah ibn Buraydah related to me, from his father, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was delivering a sermon when al-Hasan and al-Husayn came, wearing two red shirts, stumbling. The Prophet (peace be upon him) came down to them, took them, placed them in his lap on the pulpit, and said: "Allah has spoken the truth: ﴿Indeed, your wealth and your children are only a trial﴾. ﴿So fear Allah as much as you are able﴾: this abrogates (nāsikhah, naskh) His saying ﴿Fear Allah as He deserves to be feared﴾, which has already been mentioned.

﴿So fear Allah as much as you are able﴾: this abrogates (nāsikhah, naskh) His saying ﴿Fear Allah as He deserves to be feared﴾, which has already been mentioned.

﴿And listen and obey and spend; it is better for yourselves.﴾ Its implied meaning: let the spending be better for your souls. ﴿And whoever is protected from the stinginess of his soul﴾, and its withholding from the truth, ﴿those are the successful.﴾ Ibn 'Umar said: "Stinginess is not that a man withholds his wealth; rather, stinginess is that a man covets what is not his."

﴿If you lend to Allah a good loan, He will multiply it for you and forgive you. And Allah is Appreciative and Forbearing.﴾ ﴿Knower of the unseen and the witnessed, the Exalted in Might, the Wise.﴾
